methods.label: Equality of corresponding components
methods.explanation: Vectors are equal if and only if all corresponding components are equal.
methods.levelReason: This is the elementary coordinate criterion for equality of spatial vectors; a basis theorem is unnecessary.

needsNewNodes.name: Componentwise equality of spatial vectors
needsNewNodes.description: In a fixed spatial coordinate system, two vectors are equal if and only if their three corresponding components are equal. Equality of magnitudes alone or of only one component is insufficient.
needsNewNodes.reason: The catalog covers spatial coordinate representation and equality by magnitude and direction, but lacks an explicit node for this coordinate equality criterion. The spatial basis theorem is not the target of this exercise.
